name: Arithmetic (linear) population growth
variables: P_n: population after n periods; P_0: initial; X: fixed increment per period; n: number of periods
tip: Use when growth is planned/controlled by fixed numbers, not percentages.

name: Geometric population growth
variables: r: growth rate per period as fraction (10%=0.1); discrete compounding
tip: Discrete cousin of exponential; for same r, geometric < exponential.

name: Exponential population growth
variables: r: continuous growth rate; n: time
tip: India census series often fit exponential with high R^2.

name: IPAT environmental impact
formula: I = P x A x T
variables: I: impact; P: population; A: affluence (e.g. kWh/cap); T: technology factor (e.g. kg CO2/kWh)
example: CO2/y = Pop x fossil kWh/cap-y x kg CO2/kWh
tip: Growth rates roughly add in % terms when factors multiply.

name: Ecological footprint of production
variables: P: production/harvest (t/y); Y_w: world-avg yield (t/ha-y); EQF: equivalence factor
example: Convert crop tonnes to global hectares via yield and EQF
tip: Footprint is demand; compare to biocapacity (supply).

name: Energy Performance Index
variables: E_annual: kWh/year; A_floor: m^2; EPI in kWh/m^2-y
example: Campus bills summed over year / built-up area
tip: Use 3-5 years of bills for a stable EPI.

name: Betz limit / max wind power
variables: rho: air density (kg/m^3); A: rotor swept area (m^2); v: wind speed (m/s); C_P: power coefficient
example: r=25 m, v=50 km/h, rho=1.21 -> compute P_max then apply CF
tip: Memorize 16/27 ~ 59.3% and P proportional to v^3.

name: Power in the wind (kinetic flux)
variables: Before applying C_P; available power in airflow through area A
example: Double v -> 8x power
tip: Site selection cares more about wind speed than area.

name: Geothermal heat transfer
variables: m_dot: mass flow; c_p: specific heat; DeltaT: well-head minus datum temperature
tip: Convert L/s to kg/y using density at stated T.

name: Mean wave energy density
variables: H: wave height; rho: seawater density; g: gravity; E per unit sea surface
example: Used before multiplying by group velocity for power
tip: Energy proportional to H^2 -- height errors dominate.

name: Deep-water wave power (per unit crest)
variables: T: period; H: height; for deep water with c_g = c_d/2
example: H=3 m, wavelength=20 m, c=5 m/s -> T=4 s -> ~35.5 kW/m
tip: Multiply by inlet width and efficiency for device power.

name: Hydropower potential energy / efficiency
formula: PE = m g z; e_hydro = P_elec / (m_dot g z)
variables: z: operating head; m_dot: mass flow rate; P_elec: electric power output
example: 150 MW, z=35 m, Q=500 m^3/s, rho=1000 -> e_hydro = P/(m_dot g z)
tip: Head and flow dominate; kinetic of free river often negligible behind dam.

name: Tidal energy resource idea
formula: Exploit tidal range (potential) or tidal stream KE when v >= 1.5-2 m/s
variables: Range: height difference high-low tide; stream: flow speed
example: Global tidal theoretical potential ~1200 TWh/y (course)
tip: Spring tides when Sun-Moon-Earth aligned; neap when 90 deg.

name: Sound pressure level
variables: P_rms: root-mean-square sound pressure (Pa)
example: 10x pressure -> +20 dB; 10x intensity -> +10 dB
tip: 0 dB is the reference threshold of hearing, not absolute silence.

name: Sound wavelength
variables: c: speed of sound; f: frequency (Hz); also period p=1/f
example: c~343 m/s, f=343 Hz -> lambda=1 m
tip: c ~ 20.05 * sqrt(T) with T in kelvin.

name: Inverse square law (point source)
variables: W: sound power; r: distance; free-field point source
example: Double distance -> Delta L ~ -6 dB
tip: Line sources (roads): use ~-3 dB per distance doubling.

name: Combining equal sound levels
formula: Two equal incoherent sources -> L + 3 dB
variables: Energy sum: L_tot = 10 log(10^(L1/10)+10^(L2/10))
example: 50 dB + 50 dB -> 53 dB
tip: If levels differ by >=10 dB, total ~ louder source.

name: NSF Water Quality Index (concept)
variables: Q_i: sub-index from parameter chart; W_i: weight (DO 0.17, FC 0.16, ...)
example: Band: 90-100 Excellent; 0-25 Very Bad
tip: Highest weight is DO saturation.

name: Bioconcentration Factor
variables: Concentrations in tissue and water; units L/kg; rises with K_ow
example: DDT water 5e-5 ppm -> gull 6 ppm ~ BCF 1.2e5
tip: Distinguish BCF from biomagnification across trophic levels.

name: Universal Soil Loss Equation
formula: A = R K L S C P
variables: A: avg annual soil loss; R: rainfall erosivity; K: erodibility; LS: slope length/steepness; C: cover; P: practice
example: Unit plot 72.6 ft x 5.5 ft, 9% slope defines factor baselines
tip: Management levers are mainly C and P.

name: Fast pyrolysis (process note)
formula: Biomass --(400-600 C, no O2)--> bio-oil + gas + char
variables: Temperature window and anaerobic condition define product slate
example: Contrast with combustion in excess air -> CO2 + H2O + ash
tip: If O2 present it is not classical pyrolysis.

name: EGS heat extraction concept
formula: Create permeability -> circulate fluid -> extract Q=m_dot c DeltaT from hot rock
variables: Applies where natural hydrothermal productivity is poor
example: Hydraulic stimulation of hot dry rock reservoirs
tip: EGS expands geothermal beyond volcanic hydrothermal sites.

name: Logistic population growth
variables: N: population; r: intrinsic rate; K: carrying capacity
example: S-shaped approach to K vs unlimited J-curve
tip: When N << K, behaves like exponential.

name: Octanol-water partition coefficient
formula: K_ow = C_octanol / C_water; log BCF ~ f(log K_ow)
variables: Hydrophobicity proxy for organic contaminants
example: High K_ow organics bioconcentrate in fatty tissue
tip: Links chemistry to BCF exam questions.
